acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Trolls family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Scrag, T1, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Open-Wound Rebounder (Initiate) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two water construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Gangly, warty, and mud-caked with a small head, long bare arms, scavenged rags, and several half-healing gashes that never all close at once.

Signature mechanic: Bad Closure: after a committed swipe, one half-healing gash contracts into a pale bud that will restore the arm's next attack and seal some damage; interruption at the bud stops the closure and makes the arm hang slack for one cycle.
battlefieldDuty: Probe close space with long-arm swipes while one visibly open gash cycles between collapse and rapid regrowth, creating a simple interrupt-or-withdraw decision.
constructionDimensions: Regrowth becomes hydropic and bog-native: translucent fluid cysts, waterlogged callus, reed-threaded scars, shells and corroded blades sealed under wet hide, and bladderlike tissue bridges join old wounds.
Surface and motion reveal coherent pressure through swelling cysts, draining gashes, rippling scar tissue, heavy dripping limbs, and narrow fluid jets when a healing chamber ruptures.
counterplay: Step outside the preceding swipe, then strike the pale bud before the gash seals; missing that window lets the Scrag rebound immediately with the restored arm. Affinity signal: A clear cyst fills from dark to pale and a scar valve puckers before pressure moves the limb; puncturing the marked cyst drains both attack and healing into a visible low pool.
forbiddenTreatments: Palette-only water treatment without hydropic tissue, wet material response, and pressure changes
Glow-only water treatment without coherent cysts, valves, or drainage
Shapeless water bodies that remove Troll flesh, scars, and embedded objects
Opaque bog spray that conceals which cyst or wound is active
identityInvariants: Tall, stooped, potbellied humanoid silhouette with a small head on a thick neck and disproportionately long arms hanging past the knees.
Bog green, liver-brown, sallow gray, bruise purple, and wet glistening highlights keep living hide distinct from mud and scavenged rags.
Rubbery skin, scar tissue, bark-hard callus, mud, rope, and half-swallowed equipment remain visibly bodily rather than worn as deliberate finery.
Healed-over piercings, embedded bones, lodged weapons, misplaced limbs, stray jaws, and layered scars record prior injury as readable construction history.
Escalation adds accumulated misregrowth rather than simple size: open gashes become knots, alternate organs, defensive scar architecture, and finally a walking archive of incompatible healing.
telegraph: The mud-caked Scrag hunches over one always-open gash, whose rim pales and draws inward while the long attacking hand goes limp.
